name: Um
description: The GSM air interface. It carries radio resource, mobility, call control, and SMS signalling plus circuit-switched and GPRS user data between the mobile and the BTS.

name: Abis
description: The link between a BTS and its BSC. It carries radio control commands, measurement reports, and the traffic channels for the cells served by the BTS.

name: A
description: The circuit-switched interface between the GSM access network and the MSC. It carries call setup, mobility, and handover signalling and the voice bearers.

name: Gb
description: The GPRS interface between the GSM access network and the SGSN. It carries LLC frames with user data and GMM/SM signalling, plus flow control and paging.

name: Uu
description: The UMTS air interface. It carries RRC signalling with the RNC, NAS signalling with the core, and user data for CS and PS services.

name: Iub
description: The interface between a NodeB and its controlling RNC. It carries cell and radio link configuration and the frame protocol that transports user data.

name: Iur
description: The interface between two RNCs. It supports soft handover and relocation by letting a serving RNC use radio links controlled by a drift RNC.

name: Iu-CS
description: The circuit-switched interface between UTRAN and the MSC. It carries RANAP signalling for call setup, mobility, and relocation, and the CS user plane.

name: Iu-PS
description: The packet-switched interface between UTRAN and the SGSN. It carries RANAP signalling for RAB setup and relocation, and GTP-U user data tunnels.

name: LTE-Uu
description: The LTE air interface. It carries RRC signalling with the eNodeB, NAS signalling relayed to the MME, and user data on data radio bearers.

name: X2
description: The interface between neighbouring eNodeBs. It carries handover preparation, load and interference coordination, and dual connectivity signalling, and forwards user data during handover.

name: S1-MME
description: The control interface between the eNodeB and the MME. It carries UE context and E-RAB setup, paging, handover signalling, and transports NAS messages between the UE and the MME.

name: S1-U
description: The user-plane interface between the eNodeB and the SGW. It carries per-bearer GTP-U tunnels with the UE's uplink and downlink packets.

name: S3
description: The link between an SGSN and an MME. It exchanges UE context and bearer information for idle- and connected-mode mobility between 2G/3G and LTE.

name: S4
description: The interface between an SGSN and the SGW. It carries bearer control and user data for 2G/3G access anchored in the EPC.

name: S5
description: The interface between the SGW and PGW within one network. It carries bearer and PDN connection management and the user-plane tunnels; a PMIPv6 variant also exists.

name: S8
description: The roaming form of S5, between a visited-network SGW and a home-network PGW. It carries the same bearer signalling and user tunnels across PLMN borders.

name: S10
description: The interface between two MMEs. It transfers UE context during MME relocation, for example in tracking area update or handover.

name: S11
description: The control interface between the MME and the SGW. It creates, modifies, and deletes sessions and bearers, and carries downlink data notifications that trigger paging.

name: S12
description: An optional user-plane path between UTRAN and the SGW when direct tunnel bypasses the SGSN. It carries GTP-U user data tunnels.

name: SGi
description: The interface between the PGW and an external or operator packet data network. It carries the UE's IP traffic, and may use RADIUS or Diameter toward external AAA servers.

name: Sv
description: The interface between the MME and an MSC server used for single radio voice call continuity. It requests the CS side to prepare a handover when an IMS voice call moves from LTE to 2G/3G.

name: SGs
description: The interface between the MME and the MSC/VLR for CS fallback and SMS over SGs. It handles combined location updates, CS paging, and transfer of SMS for LTE-attached UEs.

name: Sm
description: The interface between the MBMS-GW and the MME. It carries MBMS session start, update, and stop signalling so the MME can set up broadcast in the radio network.

name: SBc
description: The interface between the CBC and the MME. It carries public warning messages that the MME distributes to eNodeBs for cell broadcast.

name: S6a
description: The interface between the MME and the HSS. It carries authentication vector requests, location updates, subscription data download, and purge and cancel location procedures.

name: S6d
description: The SGSN counterpart of S6a. It lets an S4-SGSN fetch authentication data and subscription profiles from the HSS over Diameter rather than MAP.

name: S13
description: The interface between the MME and the EIR. It checks the device IMEI and returns whether the equipment is allowed, blocked, or tracked.

name: S13'
description: The SGSN version of S13. It performs the same equipment identity check against the EIR using Diameter.

name: Gx
description: The policy interface between the PCEF in the PGW or GGSN and the PCRF. The PCRF installs, modifies, and removes PCC rules, and the PCEF reports IP-CAN session events and usage.

name: Gxa
description: The interface between a BBERF in a trusted non-3GPP access gateway and the PCRF. It provisions QoS rules for bearer binding when the access uses PMIPv6 or DSMIPv6.

name: Gxc
description: The interface between the BBERF in an SGW and the PCRF, used when S5/S8 is based on PMIPv6. It carries QoS rules so the SGW can bind flows to bearers.

name: Sd
description: The interface between the TDF and the PCRF. The PCRF installs application detection and control rules, and the TDF reports the start and stop of detected applications.

name: St
description: The interface between the PCRF and the TSSF. It carries traffic steering control rules that tell the TSSF which service chain to apply to detected traffic.

name: Sy
description: The interface between the PCRF and the OCS. The PCRF subscribes to spending limit counters and the OCS reports their status so policy can change when a limit is reached.

name: S9
description: The roaming interface between a home and a visited PCRF. It carries policy and QoS rules for UEs whose traffic breaks out locally or whose BBERF sits in the visited network.

name: Rx
description: The interface between an application function, such as the P-CSCF, and the PCRF. The AF describes session media so the PCRF can authorize QoS, and the PCRF reports bearer and access events back.

name: Np
description: The interface between the RCAF and the PCRF. It reports RAN user-plane congestion levels for the UEs in congested cells.

name: Nt
description: The interface between the SCEF and the PCRF. It lets a third party negotiate a background data transfer policy for a group of UEs.

name: Ns
description: The interface between the SCEF and the RCAF. The SCEF requests network status, such as congestion, for a geographic area on behalf of a service provider.

name: Gy
description: The online charging interface between the PCEF and the OCS. It carries credit control requests that reserve quota and report usage for data sessions.

name: Gz
description: The offline charging interface between the gateway and the OFCS. It carries accounting records for data sessions; a GTP' variant toward the CGF also exists.

name: Ro
description: The online charging interface between a charging trigger function, such as an IMS application server or MRFC, and the OCS. It reserves and deducts credit for sessions and events.

name: Rf
description: The offline charging interface between IMS nodes and the charging data function. It carries accounting start, interim, stop, and event records for sessions.

name: S2a
description: The interface between trusted non-3GPP access and the PGW. It sets up PDN connections and carries user tunnels for UEs on trusted WLAN; a PMIPv6 variant also exists.

name: S2b
description: The interface between the ePDG and the PGW. It sets up PDN connections and carries user tunnels for UEs on untrusted non-3GPP access, for example VoWiFi.

name: S2c
description: A host-based mobility interface between the UE and the PGW. The UE registers its care-of address with the PGW acting as home agent over trusted or untrusted non-3GPP access.

name: SWa
description: The interface between an untrusted non-3GPP access network and the 3GPP AAA Server. It carries access authentication and authorization for the WLAN itself.

name: STa
description: The interface between trusted non-3GPP access and the 3GPP AAA Server. It carries EAP-based access authentication and returns authorization data such as allowed APNs and mobility parameters.

name: SWd
description: The roaming interface between a visited 3GPP AAA Proxy and the home 3GPP AAA Server. It relays the STa, SWa, SWm, and S6b signalling of roaming UEs.

name: SWm
description: The interface between the ePDG and the 3GPP AAA Server. It carries EAP-AKA authentication of the UE during tunnel setup and returns tunnel authorization data.

name: SWn
description: The path between an untrusted non-3GPP access network and the ePDG. It carries the UE's IPsec tunnel traffic toward the ePDG.

name: SWu
description: The secure tunnel between the UE and the ePDG. It carries IKEv2 tunnel setup with EAP-AKA authentication and then the UE's user traffic inside IPsec.

name: SWx
description: The interface between the 3GPP AAA Server and the HSS. It carries authentication vector requests, registration of the serving AAA Server, and non-3GPP subscription profile download.

name: S6b
description: The interface between the PGW and the 3GPP AAA Server. The PGW registers its identity for a PDN connection and can fetch mobility parameters and authorization data.

name: SLg
description: The interface between the GMLC and the MME. The GMLC requests a UE's location, and the MME returns the estimate or reports location events such as emergency calls.

name: SLh
description: The interface between the GMLC and the HSS. It returns the address of the serving MME or SGSN for a UE whose location is requested.

name: SLs
description: The interface between the MME and the E-SMLC. It carries location requests and responses and transports LPP and LPPa positioning messages.

name: Lg
description: The MAP interface between the GMLC and the serving MSC or SGSN. It carries location requests and location reports for 2G/3G UEs.

name: Lh
description: The MAP interface between the GMLC and the HLR. It returns routing information for location requests, such as the address of the serving MSC or SGSN.

name: T6a
description: The interface between the SCEF and the MME. It carries monitoring event configuration and reports and non-IP data delivery for IoT devices.

name: T6b
description: The SGSN version of T6a. It carries monitoring events and non-IP data between the SCEF and the SGSN.

name: S6t
description: The interface between the SCEF and the HSS. It configures monitoring events, receives event reports, and provisions communication pattern parameters for UEs.

name: S6m
description: The interface between the MTC-IWF and the HSS. It maps external device identifiers to IMSI or MSISDN and returns serving node information for device triggering.

name: S6n
description: The interface between the MTC-AAA and the HSS. It maps a device's IMSI to its external identifiers for authentication and authorization of machine-type devices on non-3GPP access.

name: Tsp
description: The interface between a Services Capability Server and the MTC-IWF. It carries device trigger requests and delivery reports.

name: T4
description: The interface between the MTC-IWF and the SMS-SC. It submits device trigger requests for delivery to the UE as short messages and returns delivery reports. The SMS-IWMSC also uses it to pass MSISDN-less MO SMS to the MTC-IWF with the SGd application.

name: S6c
description: The interface between the HSS and the central SMS functions: the SMS-GMSC, SMS-IWMSC, and SMS Router, with the IP-SM-GW also reporting delivery status. It returns routing information for mobile-terminated SMS, records delivery failures as message waiting data, and alerts the SMS centre when a UE becomes reachable.

name: SGd
description: The interface between the MME and the SMS-GMSC, SMS-IWMSC, or an SMS Router, for SMS in MME. It carries mobile-originated and mobile-terminated short messages without CS fallback, and the MME uses it to alert the SMS-GMSC when a UE with pending MT SMS becomes available.

name: Gdd
description: The Diameter equivalent of Gd between the SGSN and the SMS-GMSC, SMS-IWMSC, or an SMS Router. It carries MO and MT short messages for UEs served by the SGSN and lets the SGSN alert the SMS-GMSC.

name: Gmb
description: The interface between the GGSN and the BM-SC. It carries MBMS user authorization and session start and stop for 3G broadcast and multicast.

name: SGmb
description: The control interface between the BM-SC and the MBMS-GW. It carries MBMS session start, update, and stop for EPS broadcast.

name: SGi-mb
description: The user-plane interface between the BM-SC and the MBMS-GW. It carries the broadcast content that the MBMS-GW forwards to eNodeBs.

name: Gn
description: The interface between GPRS support nodes in the same network. It carries PDP context management and user data tunnels between the SGSN and GGSN, and also SGSN-to-SGSN context transfer.

name: Gp
description: The roaming form of Gn between a visited SGSN and a home GGSN. It carries the same GTP signalling and user tunnels across PLMN borders.

name: Gi
description: The interface between the GGSN and an external packet data network. It carries the UE's IP traffic and may use RADIUS toward external AAA servers.

name: Gr
description: The MAP interface between the SGSN and the HLR. It carries authentication data requests, GPRS location updates, and subscription data insertion.

name: Gc
description: An optional MAP interface between the GGSN and the HLR. It lets the GGSN find the serving SGSN for network-requested PDP context activation.

name: Gf
description: The MAP interface between the SGSN and the EIR. It checks the IMEI of a device attaching to GPRS.

name: Gs
description: An optional interface between the SGSN and the MSC/VLR. It coordinates combined GPRS and CS attach and location updates and lets the MSC page through the SGSN.

name: Gd
description: The MAP interface between the SGSN and the SMS-GMSC or SMS-IWMSC. It carries short messages over GPRS.

name: B
description: The interface between the MSC and its VLR. It is usually internal because the two are co-located, and covers access to subscriber and location data for calls.

name: C
description: The MAP interface between a gateway MSC and the HLR. It obtains routing information for incoming calls and short messages.

name: D
description: The MAP interface between the VLR and the HLR. It carries location updates, subscriber data insertion, authentication data requests, and cancel location.

name: E
description: The MAP interface between two MSCs. It carries inter-MSC handover signalling and short message transfer between gateway and serving MSCs.

name: F
description: The MAP interface between the MSC and the EIR. It checks the IMEI of a device using CS services.

name: G
description: The MAP interface between two VLRs. A new VLR uses it to fetch the IMSI and authentication data from the previous VLR after a location change.

name: Gm
description: The SIP interface between the UE and the P-CSCF. It carries registration, session setup, and other SIP signalling, protected by IPsec or TLS.

name: Mw
description: The SIP interface between CSCFs, including P-CSCF to I-CSCF and I-CSCF to S-CSCF. It carries registration and session signalling through the IMS core.

name: Cx
description: The interface between the I-CSCF or S-CSCF and the HSS. It carries S-CSCF assignment queries, authentication vector requests, and user profile download at registration.

name: Dx
description: The interface between a CSCF and the SLF. It returns the HSS that holds a given user's data in networks with several HSSs.

name: Sh
description: The interface between an IMS application server and the HSS. It reads and updates transparent and service data for a user and subscribes to data change notifications.

name: Dh
description: The interface between an application server and the SLF. It locates the HSS that holds a user's data before the AS uses Sh.

name: ISC
description: The SIP interface between the S-CSCF and an application server. The S-CSCF sends requests to the AS when initial filter criteria match, so the AS can provide its service.

name: Ma
description: The SIP interface between the I-CSCF and an application server. It routes requests addressed to a public service identity hosted directly by the AS.

name: Ut
description: The interface between the UE and an application server for service settings. The UE reads and changes configuration such as call forwarding using XCAP, often authenticated with GBA.

name: Mg
description: The SIP interface between the MGCF and a CSCF. It carries sessions arriving from the CS network into IMS.

name: Mi
description: The SIP interface between a CSCF and the BGCF. The S-CSCF uses it to hand off sessions that must break out to the CS network.

name: Mj
description: The SIP interface between the BGCF and an MGCF in the same network. It forwards sessions that the BGCF has chosen to break out locally.

name: Mk
description: The SIP interface between BGCFs in different networks. It forwards sessions that should break out in another network.

name: Mr
description: The SIP interface between the S-CSCF and the MRFC. It requests media resources such as announcements or conferences.

name: Mr'
description: The SIP interface between an application server and the MRFC. The AS requests media resources directly, without going through the S-CSCF.

name: Mp
description: The media control interface between the MRFC and the MRFP. It allocates and controls media streams for playing, recording, and mixing.

name: Mn
description: The media gateway control interface between the MGCF and the IMS-MGW. It sets up the bearer and codec conversion between IMS and CS media.

name: Mx
description: The SIP interface between a CSCF or BGCF and the IBCF. It routes sessions to and from the network border for interconnection with other IMS networks.

name: Ici
description: The SIP interconnect between IBCFs of two IMS networks. It carries inter-operator session signalling.

name: Zh
description: The interface between the GBA bootstrapping server and the HSS. It fetches authentication vectors and GBA user security settings for bootstrapping.

name: Zn
description: The interface between a NAF and the BSF. The NAF presents a bootstrapping transaction identifier and receives the application-specific key for that UE; an HTTP variant also exists.

name: Ub
description: The interface between the UE and the BSF. It runs AKA over HTTP to create the shared GBA key and transaction identifier.

name: Ua
description: The application interface between the UE and a NAF, secured with keys derived from GBA bootstrapping.

name: NR-Uu
description: The NR air interface. It carries RRC signalling with the gNB and user data on data radio bearers, with NAS carried transparently toward the AMF.

name: Xn
description: The interface between NG-RAN nodes. It carries handover preparation, dual connectivity, and RAN paging signalling, and forwards user data during mobility.

name: N1
description: The NAS reference point between the UE and the AMF. It carries registration, mobility, and security procedures, and transports session management and SMS messages that the AMF relays to the SMF or SMSF.

name: N2
description: The control reference point between the access network and the AMF. It carries UE context and PDU session resource setup, paging, handover, and NAS transport.

name: N3
description: The user-plane reference point between the access network and the UPF. It carries per-PDU-session GTP-U tunnels with QoS flow marking.

name: N4
description: The reference point between the SMF and the UPF. The SMF installs packet detection, forwarding, QoS, and usage reporting rules, and the UPF reports usage and events.

name: N6
description: The reference point between the UPF and a data network. It carries the UE's IP, Ethernet, or unstructured traffic to and from the DN.

name: N9
description: The user-plane reference point between two UPFs, for example an intermediate UPF and a PDU session anchor, or visited and home UPFs in roaming.

name: N5
description: The reference point between an application function and the PCF. It uses Npcf_PolicyAuthorization so the AF can request QoS for its sessions and subscribe to bearer events.

name: N7
description: The reference point between the SMF and the PCF. It uses Npcf_SMPolicyControl to provide session management policy and PCC rules for PDU sessions.

name: N8
description: The reference point between the AMF and the UDM. It uses Nudm_UECM to register the serving AMF and Nudm_SDM to fetch access and mobility subscription data.

name: N10
description: The reference point between the SMF and the UDM. It uses Nudm_UECM to register the SMF for a PDU session and Nudm_SDM to read session management subscription data.

name: N11
description: The reference point between the AMF and the SMF. It uses Nsmf_PDUSession to create and update PDU sessions and Namf_Communication to pass N1 and N2 messages.

name: N12
description: The reference point between the AMF and the AUSF. It uses Nausf_UEAuthentication to run primary authentication of the UE.

name: N13
description: The reference point between the AUSF and the UDM. It uses Nudm_UEAuthentication to obtain authentication vectors and report authentication results.

name: N14
description: The reference point between two AMFs. It uses Namf_Communication to transfer UE context during AMF change.

name: N15
description: The reference point between the AMF and the PCF. It uses Npcf_AMPolicyControl and Npcf_UEPolicyControl to deliver access and mobility policy and UE route selection policy.

name: N16
description: The reference point between SMFs, such as a visited and a home SMF in home-routed roaming. It uses Nsmf_PDUSession to manage the session across both.

name: N17
description: The reference point between the AMF and the 5G-EIR. It uses N5g-eir_EquipmentIdentityCheck to verify the device PEI.

name: N18
description: The reference point between any NF and the UDSF. It uses Nudsf_DataRepository to store and retrieve unstructured context data; the AMF is shown here as a typical client.

name: N19
description: The reference point between two PDU session anchor UPFs used for local switching in 5G LAN-type services. It carries tunnelled user traffic between members of the same group.

name: N20
description: The reference point between the AMF and the SMSF. It uses Nsmsf_SMService to activate SMS for a UE and relay SMS carried in NAS.

name: N21
description: The reference point between the SMSF and the UDM. It uses Nudm_UECM to register the SMSF and Nudm_SDM to fetch SMS subscription data.

name: N22
description: The reference point between the AMF and the NSSF. It uses Nnssf_NSSelection to determine the allowed NSSAI and the target AMF set for a UE.

name: N23
description: The reference point between the PCF and the NWDAF. It uses Nnwdaf_AnalyticsInfo and Nnwdaf_AnalyticsSubscription so the PCF can base policy on analytics.

name: N24
description: The reference point between a visited and a home PCF in roaming. It carries access, mobility, and UE policy between the two networks.

name: N26
description: The interworking reference point between the MME and the AMF. It transfers UE context during handover and idle-mode mobility between EPS and 5GS.

name: N27
description: The reference point between NRFs in visited and home networks. It uses Nnrf_NFDiscovery and Nnrf_AccessToken to discover NFs and obtain tokens across PLMNs.

name: N28
description: The reference point between the PCF and the CHF. It uses Nchf_SpendingLimitControl to subscribe to the status of spending limit counters.

name: N29
description: The reference point between the NEF and the SMF. It uses Nsmf_NIDD to carry non-IP data between an application and the UE.

name: N30
description: The reference point between the NEF and the PCF. It uses Npcf_PolicyAuthorization and Npcf_BDTPolicyControl so external applications can influence QoS and background data transfer.

name: N31
description: The reference point between NSSFs in visited and home networks. It uses Nnssf_NSSelection to map slices across PLMNs for roaming UEs.

name: N32
description: The reference point between SEPPs of two PLMNs. N32-c negotiates security capabilities and N32-f forwards protected service-based messages between the networks.

name: N33
description: The reference point between the NEF and external application functions. It exposes northbound APIs such as event monitoring, traffic influence, and parameter provisioning.

name: N34
description: The reference point between the NSSF and the NWDAF. It lets the NSSF use slice load analytics when selecting slices.

name: N35
description: The reference point between the UDM and the UDR. It uses Nudr_DataRepository to read and write subscription data.

name: N36
description: The reference point between the PCF and the UDR. It uses Nudr_DataRepository to read policy and application data and subscribe to changes.

name: N37
description: The reference point between the NEF and the UDR. It uses Nudr_DataRepository to store and read exposure and application data.

name: N40
description: The reference point between the SMF and the CHF. It uses Nchf_ConvergedCharging to report usage and request quota for PDU sessions.

name: N50
description: The reference point between the AMF and the CBCF. It uses Namf_Communication to deliver public warning messages for broadcast in NG-RAN.

name: N51
description: The reference point between the AMF and the NEF. It uses Namf_EventExposure so the NEF can monitor UE events such as reachability and location.

name: N52
description: The reference point between the NEF and the UDM. It uses Nudm_EventExposure and Nudm_ParameterProvision to set up monitoring and provision UE parameters.

name: N58
description: The reference point between the AMF and the NSSAAF. It uses Nnssaaf_NSSAA to run slice-specific authentication of the UE.

name: N59
description: The reference point between the UDM and the NSSAAF. It supports slice authentication procedures that need subscription data.

name: NWu
description: The reference point between the UE and the N3IWF over untrusted non-3GPP access. It sets up IPsec tunnels for NAS signalling and for user-plane traffic.

name: NWt
description: The reference point between the UE and the TNGF over trusted non-3GPP access. It carries NAS and user traffic inside IPsec security associations.

name: NLs
description: The reference point between the AMF and the LMF. It uses Nlmf_Location for positioning requests and Namf_Communication to carry positioning messages to the UE and NG-RAN.

name: NLg
description: The reference point between the GMLC and the AMF. It uses Namf_Location to request a UE's location and receive location event reports.

name: NLh
description: The reference point between the GMLC and the UDM. It returns the serving AMF and location privacy settings for a UE.

name: S17
description: The reference point between the MME and the UCMF for radio capability signalling optimisation (RACS). The MME uses it to resolve UE Radio Capability IDs to full capability sets and to have the UCMF assign PLMN IDs for new capability sets.

name: Iuh
description: The interface between a Home NodeB and its HNB gateway, usually carried over the public internet. It handles HNB and UE registration and relays RANAP signalling and user data toward the core.

name: Mc
description: The gateway control interface between an MSC Server or GMSC Server and a CS-MGW. The server uses it to set up terminations, bearers, and media processing in the gateway, including anchoring during handover and relocation.

name: Nc
description: The call control interface between MSC Servers and GMSC Servers in a split CS core. It carries network-to-network call signalling such as ISUP or bearer independent call control, over IP or SS7 transport.

name: Nb
description: The user plane between two CS-MGWs in a split CS core. It carries the voice and data bearers and their bearer control, using RTP over IP or AAL2 over ATM.

name: Hv
description: The reference point between the VLR and the CSS in the visited network. The CSS uses it to give the VLR the CSG subscription data it holds for roaming users so they can use CS services in CSG cells.

name: Ghv
description: The reference point between a Gn/Gp SGSN and the CSS in the visited network. It transfers the CSG subscription data held in the VPLMN for roaming users to the SGSN.

name: H
description: The internal link between the HLR or HSS and the Authentication Centre. The HLR requests authentication and ciphering vectors from the AuC when it holds none for a subscriber.

name: S14
description: The reference point between the UE and the ANDSF, carried over IP. The UE pulls, or the ANDSF pushes, access network discovery information and inter-system mobility and routing policies for non-3GPP accesses such as WLAN.

name: S101
description: The reference point between the MME and a 3GPP2 HRPD access network. It tunnels HRPD signalling for a UE on E-UTRAN, supporting pre-registration, session maintenance, and active handover to HRPD.

name: S102
description: The tunnel between the MME and a 3GPP2 1xCS interworking solution. It relays 1xRTT CS signalling for SRVCC and CS fallback to CDMA2000 1x circuit-switched networks.

name: S103
description: The user plane interface between the Serving GW and the HRPD Serving Gateway. It forwards downlink data during handover from E-UTRAN to HRPD, using tunnels set up through S101 signalling.

name: Uh
description: The reference point between the UE and the CSG List Server. It provisions the Allowed CSG list and the Operator CSG list on the UE, either by OMA DM or by OTA updates to the USIM.

name: S7d
description: The interface between an S4-SGSN and the CSS in the visited network. The CSS provides, and updates, the CSG subscription data it holds for roaming users.

name: S7a
description: The interface between the MME and the CSS in the visited network. The CSS provides, and updates, the CSG subscription data it holds for roaming users so the MME can control access to CSG cells.

name: S121
description: The reference point between the MME and a 3GPP2 HRPD access network for RAN information management. It relays RIM messages between eNodeBs and the HRPD access network, for example to exchange cell load information.

name: I
description: The interface between an MSC and its Group Call Register. The MSC queries the GCR for the attributes of a voice group or voice broadcast call, such as the cells and MSCs the call covers.

name: Lb
description: The GERAN interface between the BSC and a standalone SMLC. It carries positioning requests, measurements, and location results for the target MS served by the BSC; in UTRAN the SMLC role sits in the SRNC.

name: Lp
description: The GERAN interface between peer SMLCs. An SMLC uses it to reach positioning information and resources, such as LMUs, owned by another SMLC; in UTRAN the equivalent function runs over Iur.

name: Le
description: The interface between an external LCS client and the GMLC. The client requests a target UE's location and receives the estimate, typically using the OMA Mobile Location Protocol or the OSA API.

name: Iupc
description: The UTRAN interface between the SRNC and a Stand-Alone SMLC. The SAS supplies positioning assistance data to the RNC and can calculate the UE's position from measurements the RNC passes on.

name: Lr
description: The interface between GMLCs, often across networks when the target UE is roaming. It forwards location requests and results between the requesting, home, and visited GMLCs.

name: Lgd
description: The interface between the GMLC and an SGSN that supports EPS-based protocols. The GMLC sends location requests for a UE the SGSN serves, and the SGSN returns the location results.

name: Ge
description: The CAMEL interface between the gprsSSF in the SGSN and the gsmSCF. The gprsSSF asks for instructions, and the gsmSCF then controls the GPRS session or PDP context, for example for prepaid charging.

name: Iu-BC
description: The interface between the Cell Broadcast Centre and the UTRAN RNC. It carries cell broadcast messages and their delivery parameters, such as the cells and repetition schedule.

name: Mb
description: The IMS media plane, carried over IP between media-handling functions such as the UE, MRFP, IMS-MGW, and TrGW and toward IP networks. It transports the RTP voice, video, and other media streams of IMS sessions.

name: Si
description: The interface between the IM-SSF and the HSS. It transfers CAMEL subscription information, including trigger data, so CAMEL-based services can run for IMS sessions; the same data can also travel over Sh.

name: Ix
description: The gateway control interface between the IBCF and the TrGW at an IMS network border. The IBCF uses it to request address and port translation bindings and IPv4/IPv6 conversion for session media.

name: Iq
description: The gateway control interface between the P-CSCF and the IMS Access Gateway. The P-CSCF uses it to allocate and release media transport addresses and to set policing and NAT traversal for each flow.

name: Izi
description: The media path between TrGWs that belong to different IMS networks. It forwards the RTP media streams of sessions that cross an IMS-to-IMS interconnect, after address and protocol translation.

name: I2
description: The reference point between an MSC Server and the IMS CSCFs, usable across operators. It routes SIP session control for an MSC Server enhanced for ICS or SRVCC, including mid-call and alerting-phase transfer.

name: I3
description: The reference point between an MSC Server enhanced for ICS and the telephony application server. It interworks CS supplementary service signalling and service setting procedures with the TAS.

name: I1
description: The reference point between an ICS UE and the SCC AS. It carries IMS service control signalling while the UE uses CS access for the call bearer.

name: Ms
description: The reference point between an IBCF and an application server. The IBCF uses it for caller identity attestation, identity signing, and signature verification on calls crossing the network border.

name: Wa
description: The I-WLAN reference point between a WLAN access network and the 3GPP AAA Proxy or Server. It carries authentication, authorization, and charging data for WLAN access.

name: Wd
description: The I-WLAN roaming reference point between the visited 3GPP AAA Proxy and the home 3GPP AAA Server. It relays authentication, authorization, and related information for roaming WLAN users.

name: Wg
description: The I-WLAN reference point between the 3GPP AAA Server or Proxy and the WAG. It gives the WAG the policy enforcement information for authorised users and returns per-tunnel charging data when roaming.

name: Wi
description: The I-WLAN reference point between the PDG and a packet data network. The network can be an external public or private network or an operator network, for example for IMS services.

name: Wm
description: The I-WLAN reference point between the 3GPP AAA Server or Proxy and the PDG. It carries service authentication and authorization, tunnel authentication data, and tunnelling attributes and IP configuration for the WLAN UE.

name: Wn
description: The I-WLAN reference point between the WLAN access network and the WAG. It forces traffic between a WLAN UE and the PDG to pass through the WAG.

name: Wp
description: The I-WLAN reference point between the WAG and the PDG. It transports the tunnelled Wu packets between the WLAN UE and the PDG, so the WAG can enforce policy on them.

name: Wu
description: The I-WLAN reference point between the WLAN UE and the PDG. The UE uses it to set up a tunnel to the PDG and exchange packet data with 3GPP PS services through it.

name: Ww
description: The I-WLAN reference point between the WLAN UE and the WLAN access network. Its radio and access protocols, such as 802.11 and 802.1X, are defined by IEEE outside 3GPP.

name: Wx
description: The I-WLAN reference point between the 3GPP AAA Server and the HSS. The AAA Server fetches authentication vectors, WLAN subscriber profiles, and charging addresses, and registers itself for authorised WLAN users.

name: Dw
description: The reference point between the 3GPP AAA Server and the SLF. The AAA Server uses it to find which HSS holds a user's data when the network has several HSSs.

name: Mz
description: The roaming variant of Gmb, between a BM-SC in the visited network and one in the home network. It carries MBMS service authorization and bearer signalling for roaming users.

name: Gmc
description: The reference point between the GGSN and the RNS or Iu-mode BSS for MBMS. It delivers MBMS user data to the radio network using IP multicast.

name: Sn
description: The reference point between the MBMS-GW and an S4-SGSN. It carries MBMS session start, update, and stop signalling and delivers MBMS data to the SGSN in point-to-point mode.

name: M1
description: The MBMS user plane between the MBMS-GW and the E-UTRAN or UTRAN. It delivers broadcast content to the eNodeBs or RNCs over IP multicast with GTP-U encapsulation.

name: M3
description: The control interface between the MME and the MCE for E-UTRAN MBMS. It carries MBMS session start, update, and stop signalling, with the session's QoS and service area.

name: M2
description: The control interface between the MCE and the eNodeBs in an MBSFN area. It carries MBMS session control and the radio configuration the MCE allocates for the broadcast.

name: xMB
description: The reference point between a content provider and the BM-SC, either directly or through the SCEF. The provider uses it to create and control MBMS user services and to hand over the content to broadcast.

name: Rg
description: The reference point between applications and the GUP Server. Applications use it to create, read, modify, and delete Generic User Profile data, and the GUP Server locates the repositories that hold it.

name: Rp
description: The reference point from the GUP Server, or from applications, to GUP data repositories such as the HSS. It gives access to the stored user profile components, including IMS user data.

name: Sp
description: The reference point between the PCRF and the Subscription Profile Repository. The PCRF fetches subscription data for policy decisions, and the SPR can notify it when that data changes.

name: Gxb
description: The reference point between the ePDG and the PCRF or visited PCRF; only the Gxb* variant for fixed broadband interworking is specified. It reports WLAN access information such as the UE's local IP address and UDP port.

name: Gxx
description: The generic name for the policy interface between the PCRF and a BBERF, covering Gxa and Gxc. The PCRF uses it to install QoS rules and control bearer binding and event reporting in the access gateway.

name: Ud
description: The reference point between application front ends, such as HLR, HSS, or AS front ends, and the UDR in a User Data Convergence architecture. Front ends, including a PCRF acting as one, read and update user data and subscribe to change notifications.

name: S15
description: The reference point between the HNB-GW and the PCRF for fixed broadband interworking. It sets up, modifies, and ends sessions so the PCRF can request fixed network resources for HNB CS calls.

name: S9a
description: The reference point between the PCRF and the Broadband Policy Control Function of a fixed broadband access network. It transfers QoS policy information from the PCRF to the BPCF.

name: Gyn
description: The online charging interface between the TDF and the OCS. It uses Diameter credit control to request quota and report usage for the application traffic the TDF detects.

name: Gzn
description: The offline charging interface between the TDF and the OFCS. It transfers charging data and records for the application traffic the TDF detects, for later billing.

name: Gw
description: The reference point between the PFDF and the PCEF. The PFDF provides the Packet Flow Descriptions that third parties manage, so the PCEF can detect their application traffic.

name: Gwn
description: The reference point between the PFDF and the TDF. The PFDF provides the Packet Flow Descriptions that third parties manage, so the TDF can detect their application traffic.

name: J
description: The reference point between the IP-SM-GW and the HSS for SMS over IP. The IP-SM-GW uses it to register as the user's serving node for SMS and to fetch routing data.

name: Nu
description: The reference point between the SCEF and the PFDF. The SCEF adds, updates, and removes Packet Flow Descriptions in the PFDF on behalf of third-party SCS/AS providers.

name: MB2
description: The reference point between a GCS AS and the BM-SC for group communication over LTE. It starts, stops, and modifies MBMS broadcast bearers and carries the group application data to broadcast.

name: GC1
description: The application-level reference point between the UE and the GCS AS. It carries group communication signalling and application data, over unicast bearers or alongside MBMS delivery.

name: PC1
description: The application-level reference point between the ProSe application in the UE and the ProSe Application Server. Its signalling is left to the application and not specified by 3GPP.

name: PC2
description: The reference point between the ProSe Application Server and the ProSe Function. It supports EPC- level ProSe discovery, for example by translating application user identities into network identities.

name: PC3
description: The over-IP reference point between the UE and the ProSe Function. It authorises discovery requests, allocates ProSe Application Codes, and provisions per-PLMN policy for direct discovery and communication.

name: PC4a
description: The reference point between the ProSe Function and the HSS. It provides per-PLMN ProSe subscription data for authorising direct discovery and communication, and EPC-level discovery subscriber data.

name: PC4b
description: The reference point between the ProSe Function and the SUPL Location Platform. The ProSe Function acts as an LCS client and queries the SLP for UE locations during EPC-level discovery.

name: PC5
description: The direct radio link between ProSe-enabled UEs, without passing through the network. It carries control and user plane traffic for direct discovery, direct communication, and UE-to-network relay.

name: PC6
description: The reference point between ProSe Functions in different PLMNs, such as home and local. It authorises discovery requests, retrieves discovery filters, and translates ProSe Application Codes to application IDs.

name: PC7
description: The reference point between the home and visited ProSe Functions. It lets the home network control ProSe service authorization and handles discovery authorization, filters, and code translation.

name: Nq
description: The reference point between the MME and the RCAF. The RCAF retrieves the UEs served by a congested eNodeB or cell and the APNs of their active PDN connections.

name: Mm
description: The IP signalling interface between a CSCF or IBCF and external multimedia IP networks. It exchanges SIP session requests with other SIP servers or terminals outside the IMS.

name: N16a
description: The reference point between the anchor SMF and an I-SMF inserted for a PDU session. It uses Nsmf_PDUSession to pass N4 rules and QoS information that the I-SMF applies to the UPFs it controls.

name: N38
description: The reference point between I-SMFs and between V-SMFs, in the same or different PLMNs. It transfers the SM context and forwarding tunnel information when the I-SMF or V-SMF of a PDU session changes.

name: N41
description: The reference point between the AMF and the CHF in the home PLMN. It uses Nchf_ConvergedCharging to report registration, mobility, and connection events for charging.

name: N42
description: The reference point between the AMF and the CHF in the visited PLMN. It uses Nchf_ConvergedCharging so the VPLMN can charge for the registration, mobility, and connection events of roaming UEs.

name: N43
description: The reference point between the PCF for the UE and the PCF for the PDU session. It is used, for example, with Npcf_UEPolicyControl to deliver URSP rules to a UE served over EPS.

name: N55
description: The reference point between the AMF and the UCMF. It uses Nucmf_UECapabilityManagement to assign UE radio capability IDs and resolve them into full radio capabilities.

name: N56
description: The reference point between the NEF and the UCMF. It lets an external AF provision manufacturer- assigned UE radio capability IDs in the UCMF through the NEF.

name: N57
description: The reference point between a trusted AF and the UCMF. The AF uses Nucmf_Provisioning to provision manufacturer-assigned UE radio capability IDs directly, without the NEF.

name: N60
description: The reference point between the AUSF and the NSWOF. It uses Nausf_UEauthentication to authenticate a UE with its 5GS credentials when it connects to a WLAN for non-seamless offload.

name: N80
description: The reference point between the AMF and the NSACF. It uses Nnsacf_NSAC to check and update the number of UEs registered on a network slice before admitting a UE.

name: N81
description: The reference point between the SMF and the NSACF. It uses Nnsacf_NSAC to check and update the number of PDU sessions on a network slice before admitting a session.

name: N82
description: The reference point between the NSACF and the NEF. It uses Nnsacf_SliceEventExposure to report slice status, such as current UE and PDU session counts, toward an AF.

name: N83
description: The reference point between the AUSF and the NSSAAF. It uses Nnssaaf_AIW to relay EAP authentication toward an external AAA server, for example for SNPN access with credentials from a credentials holder.

name: N84
description: The reference point between the TSCTSF and the PCF. The TSCTSF uses Npcf_PolicyAuthorization to pass QoS requirements, TSC assistance containers, and time synchronization settings for a PDU session.

name: N85
description: The reference point between the TSCTSF and the NEF. The NEF relays external AF requests for time synchronization and time sensitive QoS to the TSCTSF services.

name: N86
description: The reference point between the TSCTSF and a trusted AF. The AF uses the TSCTSF services directly to request time synchronization and QoS for time sensitive traffic.

name: N87
description: The reference point between the TSCTSF and the UDM. The TSCTSF uses Nudm_SDM to fetch time synchronization subscription data and to resolve GPSIs and group IDs into SUPIs.

name: N88
description: The reference point between the SMF and the EASDF. The SMF uses Neasdf_DNSContext to install rules for handling a PDU session's DNS messages and to receive DNS message reports.

name: N89
description: The reference point between the TSCTSF and the AMF. The TSCTSF subscribes to UE presence in an area of interest and sends non-UE N2 messages to configure and monitor NG-RAN time synchronization.

name: N96
description: The reference point between the TSCTSF and the NRF. The TSCTSF uses Nnrf_NFDiscovery, for example to find the AMFs serving the tracking areas of a time synchronization coverage area.

name: N97
description: The reference point between NSACFs in different PLMNs. A VPLMN NSACF uses it to reach the HPLMN primary or central NSACF for slice admission control of inbound roamers.

name: N99
description: The reference point between NSACFs in the same PLMN. In a hierarchical deployment, NSACFs use it to obtain and return slice quota from the primary NSACF.

name: Sxa
description: The reference point between the SGW-C and the SGW-U. The SGW-C installs packet detection, forwarding, and buffering rules, and the SGW-U reports usage and downlink data arrival for idle UEs.

name: Sxb
description: The reference point between the PGW-C and the PGW-U. The PGW-C installs detection, forwarding, QoS, and usage reporting rules for bearers. In 5GS interworking, a PGW-C+SMF uses N4 toward a UPF+PGW-U instead.

name: Sxc
description: The reference point between the TDF-C and the TDF-U. The TDF-C installs application detection and enforcement rules, and the TDF-U reports detected applications and usage.

name: Sxa/Sxb
description: The reference point between the control and user plane functions of a combined SGW/PGW. It uses the same Sx parameter structure and covers only the functionality of Sxa and Sxb.

name: S11-U
description: The user-plane reference point between the MME and the SGW, used for Control Plane CIoT EPS Optimisation. It carries user data sent in NAS messages; with CUPS it terminates on the SGW-U.

name: F1-C
description: The control-plane interface between the gNB-CU-CP and a gNB-DU. It carries F1AP over SCTP for UE context management, RRC message transfer, system information, and cell management.

name: F1-U
description: The user-plane interface between the gNB-CU-UP and a gNB-DU. It carries user data for each data radio bearer in GTP-U tunnels, with flow control feedback from the DU.

name: E1
description: The interface between the gNB-CU-CP and the gNB-CU-UP. The CU-CP uses E1AP to set up, modify, and release bearer contexts in the CU-UP for each UE.

name: Ga
description: The offline charging interface between the CDF and the CGF. It carries CDRs over GTP' (GTP prime), which the CGF then validates, consolidates, and passes to the billing domain.
